chunks: 'Ali, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Talhah al-Nahdi, from Sawrah ibn Kulayb, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: A man goes out from his house intending the mosque, or intending some need, then a man meets him or follows him, strikes him, and takes his garment. So he said: “What do those with you say about it?”

I said: They say, “This is open brigandage, and the muharib is only in polytheist settlements.” So he said: “Which of the two has greater sanctity: the abode of Islam or the abode of shirk?” He said: I said: The abode of Islam.
So he said: “These are among the people meant by this verse: ‘إِنَّمَا جَزَاءُ الَّذِينَ يُحَارِبُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ’ to the end of the verse.”

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque, mentioned as the destination of the victim
key_terms.الْمُحَارِبُ: one who wages war; here, a violent offender subject to the verse's ruling
key_terms.دَارُ الشِّرْكِ: the abode of shirk, contrasted with the abode of Islam
key_terms.دَارُ الْإِسْلَامِ: the abode of Islam, whose sanctity the Imam عليه السلام emphasizes
key_terms.يُحَارِبُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ: they wage war against Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم; the Qur'anic phrase applied here

ai.seo_question: Does violent robbery in Muslim lands count as muharabah under the Qur'an?
ai.summary: This hadith applies the Qur'anic ruling on those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم to violent robbery committed within the abode of Islam. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rejects limiting the term muharib to hostile non-Muslim territories and affirms that such aggression in Muslim lands falls under the verse's legal scope.
